original.guitar: Charlie Starr: Les Paul Junior (P-90), Fender Esquire / B-Bender Telecaster; Paul Jackson: Les Paul
original.amp: Tweed Deluxe-style combo (Echopark Vibramatic) blended with a Marshall-style head (Germino) into a 4x12
original.effects: Mostly straight into the amp; Klon-style boost, spring reverb
original.notes: No source documents the exact settings for this song. Built from the band's published rigs.

recipes.tips: Channel A is the tweed rhythm sound for the verses. Switch to channel B for a bigger Marshall-style crunch in the choruses. If it needs more push, stomp the Tube OD: it works as a light, Klon-style boost.
recipes.why: Starr runs a tweed Deluxe-style amp all the time and blends it with a Marshall-style head. Channel A copies the tweed, channel B the Marshall. A split Pearly Gates on the bridge gets close to his Esquire and P-90 bite.

sources.title: Premier Guitar: Rig Rundown, Blackberry Smoke (2023)

original.guitar: B-Bender Telecaster (the intro riff and solo use B-string bender bends)
original.amp: Marshall-style head (Germino) into a 4x12, with the tweed combo blended in
original.effects: Klon-style boost, a little delay, spring reverb
original.notes: No source documents the exact settings for this song. Built from the band's published rigs.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the intro riff, channel B for the solo. You don't have a B-bender, so fake the bends: bend the B string up a whole step while you hold the high E (or G) note still, or pre-bend it and let it down. Keep the tone knob pulled for single-coil twang.
recipes.why: A Plexi-style crunch over a 4x12, pushed by a light overdrive, keeps the bends round but cutting. A short analog slapback and spring reverb fill out the sound without blurring the notes.

sources.title: Premier Guitar: Rig Rundown, Blackberry Smoke (2023)
